data.narrative:
Standard Bots, a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Evan Beard and David Golden, has raised $200M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 3 same-stage, same-sector private comparables (Generalist AI at $2.0B, Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B, and Dexterity at $1.6B), supplemented by a broader universe of 8 private companies and 1 public comparable in the sector.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a base proxy and applying a typical 1.9x Series B step-up multiplier, implies a valuation of $380M. Peer-median methodology across the three same-stage, same-sector comparables yields $1.8B, with a range spanning $1.6B to $2.0B. These methods diverge substantially, reflecting uncertainty around whether Standard Bots trades at a discount to or in line with robotics sector peers.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $323M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $1.1B. The wide spread reflects tension between the stage-progression method—anchored conservatively to capital deployed—and peer medians influenced by elevated valuations in early-stage robotics. Key uncertainties include Standard Bots' revenue scale and growth trajectory relative to peers, and whether the peer set adequately reflects market conditions at time of this company's next financing event.
